checkpoints.description: Task 'sanctuary-buildings' completed successfully.

[1/4] Plan: add two mechanical Sanctuary places - The Reliquary (attune one owned relic to start every expedition) and The Cairn (spend echoes to bank starting shards) - and give each resident room its own palette, lighting and themed environment props so the five interiors read as five different places

impact_assessment.why: the hub currently has four places and the rooms share one sanctuary palette, so they look like the same room with different furniture
impact_assessment.benefits: two more long-term decisions in the hub and five visually distinct interiors built from one art pipeline
impact_assessment.risks: contract: SanctuaryStation ids, Meta schema defaults, LevelView/tileTextures optional theme, createExpedition starting shards; dependency: generated props; concurrency: single-threaded; state: new Meta fields need defaults so old saves load
impact_assessment.mitigation: add every new Meta field with a zod default, keep station ids additive, test attunement/offerings as pure functions, verify each room with Playwright screenshots and one vision reviewer

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Delivered: two mechanical places (Reliquary attunement, Cairn echo offerings) with tests and meta defaults; five interiors now use distinct biome materials plus themed furniture sets and eight new generated props; hub cards carry prop badges; a single vision review drove fixes for label collision, hint contrast, floating/clipping props, glyph bleed and CTA contrast. 135 tests, 7/7 gates pass. checklists: passed
Task 'sanctuary-polish' completed successfully.

[4/4] Delivered: eighth and final Sanctuary place The Reforge (3 ranks, 30/60/100 echoes, +12% per rank on relic mods, carried by EquipmentItem.rank), hub capped at exactly 8 places in a balanced 4x2 grid, per-room floor grammar (archive ring, forge cracks, garden moss, barracks drill lines, lamp pools), three new props (desk, cauldron, lamp strings), and a U+FFFD encoding regression test after a corrupted middle dot in the Reforge button. Verified by DOM/world measurement: 8 stations aligned in 4 rows, footer within 720, no card overflow, no prop outside its room or on the door lane; 147 tests and 7/7 gates pass. checklists: passed
Task 'sanctuary-polish-2' completed successfully.

[4/4] Runtime audit of the shipped game: exercised title, hub, 8 places, 5 rooms, dialogue/quests, combat, menus, level-up, death, retry, restart, victory, and old/corrupt saves. Fixed two defects and one weak pattern: dropped sub-frame clicks/taps (attack+bolt press latches), hub column labels forced to page width, and the wall attack's fixed centre gap. Verified 3 instant right-clicks spend mana, 4 instant melee taps damage an enemy, no off-screen/clipped UI, no NaN in combat, no console errors. 150 tests, 7/7 gates. checklists: passed
Task 'runtime-audit' completed successfully.

[1/2] Plan: make Rest resume the healed expedition instead of opening Set Out, show an honest rest price, extract restCost(depth), and declare a headless mechanics contract so AIKit can test the simulation without a browser

impact_assessment.why: paying for Rest then being pushed into a fresh-run screen discarded the healed run, and the game had no headless mechanics gate
impact_assessment.benefits: rest does what its price promises, one price rule with a test, and a mechanics gate on every check
impact_assessment.risks: contract: App rest call sites, hub exports, project.json/package.json scripts; dependency: none; concurrency: single-threaded; state: no save schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: return the healed run from restSavedRun and start it at every call site, unit-test restCost, run the full and mechanics suites

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Done: Rest heals and resumes the saved run from hub, ledger and Set Out screen; hub shows 'Rest' with no price when no run exists; restCost(depth) extracted and unit-tested; mechanics contract added (src/sim, src/data, npm run test:mechanics) with mechanics_required true. Verified in Playwright: rest spends 16 echoes and resumes at 120 HP, label is plain 'Rest' without a save. 151 tests, 118 mechanics tests, 8/8 gates. checklists: passed
Task 'rest-and-mechanics' completed successfully.
[1/2] Plan: fix in-room overlays ejecting the player to the hub on Escape, document the mechanics gate in README and the agent guide, and record the verification

impact_assessment.why: Escape from the room menu, inventory or settings left the room because the menu stored state hub
impact_assessment.benefits: Escape is a real toggle everywhere and the headless gate is documented
impact_assessment.risks: contract: App menu state and closeOverlay, docs; dependency: none; concurrency: single-threaded; state: no save changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: use the paused overlay state, make closeOverlay room-aware, keep the hub root inert on Escape, and verify the exact sequences in Playwright

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Done: room menu uses paused state, closeOverlay resumes the room for sanctuary worlds, Escape closes hub sub-screens but is inert on the hub root. Verified sequences: room menu closes to room, room inventory and room settings return to room, Back to the Sanctuary still leaves, hub Escape does nothing, run inventory resumes play. Documented npm run test:mechanics in README and docs. 151 tests, 118 mechanics tests, gates pass. checklists: passed
Task 'room-overlay-fix' completed successfully.
[1/2] Plan: let Tab, Space and arrows reach DOM menus while keeping gameplay suppression, and document menu keyboard navigation

impact_assessment.why: Tab and Space were prevented for the whole session, so keyboard users could not navigate or activate any menu
impact_assessment.benefits: full keyboard access to the hub, places and all overlays
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Input keydown suppression, README controls; dependency: none; concurrency: single-threaded; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: gate suppression on the presence of a .screen, verify focus order and activation in Playwright, keep play bindings unchanged

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Done: Input suppresses Space/Tab/arrows only when no .screen is open, so menus get native focus and activation while play keeps Tab=map and Space=dash. Verified: Tab cycles five building Enter buttons then station buttons, Space opens Training Yard, Enter enters a room from its card, in-play Tab still opens the map. README documents Tab + Enter/Space. 151 tests, gates pass. checklists: passed
Task 'keyboard-menus' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: audit the run lifecycle end-to-end - death and game over, meta reward claims, save persistence across reload, cairn banked shards and attuned relic carrying into the next run; [2/3] fix any real bugs found; [3/3] verify, document and deliver

impact_assessment.why: every prior audit pass tested systems inside a live run; the loop that closes a run (death, rewards, persistence, next-run carry-over) was never driven end-to-end, so progression bugs could ship silently
impact_assessment.benefits: players cannot lose earned echoes/shards/relics on death or reload, and cairn/reliquary choices provably reach the next run
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, read-mostly audit plus targeted fixes; dependency: none beyond existing Playwright; concurrency: none; state: tests mutate localStorage in an ephemeral browser profile only
impact_assessment.mitigation: drive the game only through the public __MR__ debug handle, fix findings with unit tests first, keep edits inside the audited flow

checkpoints.description: [2/3] No bugs found: cairn 3x45 shards spent on set out, attuned echo_dagger equipped first, reforge rank 2 carried, mid-run save + title Continue restored depth/shards/equipment, death banked +67 echoes and cleared the run, abandon recorded the run, rest healed 80/120->120/120 for 16 echoes and resumed at depth 3, victory paid the +60 bonus and showed The World Remembers, meta persisted across reloads, zero console errors in three Playwright audits; [3/3] no code change needed, ledger only
Task 'run-lifecycle-audit' completed successfully.
